title: Portland Trivia Night

questions.q: Portland got its name from a coin toss in 1845. Which city's name lost the toss?
Which river runs through downtown Portland, dividing the east side from the west?
Which snow-capped volcano, the highest point in Oregon, can be seen east of Portland on a clear day?
Portland's most famous nickname is the City of what?
Portland's NBA team won its only championship in 1977. What is the team called?
Which Simpsons character, the family's next-door neighbor, shares his surname with a Portland street?
A two-foot-wide circle of ground in a Naito Parkway median is recognized by Guinness as the world's smallest what?
Complete the city's unofficial slogan, seen on bumper stickers: Keep Portland what?
Which sportswear company, founded as Blue Ribbon Sports, has its world headquarters in the Portland suburb of Beaverton?
At Portland Timbers home matches, what does the mascot Timber Joey cut with a chainsaw after every home goal?

notes: Asa Lovejoy wanted Boston, Francis Pettygrove wanted Portland; Pettygrove won the toss in 1845 with the 'Portland Penny'; see History of Portland, Oregon (Wikipedia) or the Oregon Historical Society.
The Willamette River flows north through Portland to the Columbia; see Willamette River (Wikipedia).
Mount Hood (11,249 ft) is Oregon's highest peak, about 50 miles east of Portland; see Mount Hood (Wikipedia) or USGS.
Nicknamed the City of Roses / Rose City, home of the Portland Rose Festival and International Rose Test Garden; see Portland, Oregon (Wikipedia).
Portland Trail Blazers won the 1977 NBA Finals over the 76ers, their only title; see Portland Trail Blazers (Wikipedia) or NBA.com.
Matt Groening grew up in Portland and named Flanders, Lovejoy, Quimby and others after local streets; see Northwest Flanders Street / Ned Flanders (Wikipedia).
Mill Ends Park, about 2 ft across, listed by Guinness as the smallest park in the world since 1971; see Mill Ends Park (Wikipedia) or Portland Parks & Recreation.
'Keep Portland Weird' slogan, adopted from Austin's 'Keep Austin Weird'; see Keep Portland Weird (Wikipedia).
Nike founded 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports, renamed 1971, headquartered near Beaverton, Oregon; see Nike, Inc. (Wikipedia).
Timber Joey saws a slab ('log slice') off a log after each Timbers home goal and presents it to the scorer; see Portland Timbers (Wikipedia) or timbers.com.
